paragraphs: CaseWorthy sells a software platform for case and program management in human services. Its buyers are nonprofit organizations and local and state governments that deliver social care programs.

The platform pulls programs, people, data and workflows together in one system rather than scattering them across separate tools. Agencies configure their own workflows, forms, assessments and service plans to match how each program operates. Reporting for funders is built into the platform instead of assembled in spreadsheets. Underneath sits a data lakehouse called CORE that consolidates information from CaseWorthy applications and outside sources. CORE ships baseline data models for particular sectors, including HMIS for homeless services, aging services and workforce development metrics.

Beyond case management there are applications for HCBS and I/DD providers covering care coordination, scheduling and Medicaid-supported service delivery. Another handles scheduling, documentation and billing for Home and Community-Based Services agencies. An AI copilot named Cara is embedded in the platform to reduce documentation time and surface insights. The company states that the organizations it serves touch more than 41% of the US population.
